text: Writes a time that changes to the reader's own time zone. Someone in New York and someone in Stockholm both see the time in their own clock. Without JavaScript, or while the page loads, the time is shown as it was typed with its time zone. Usage {{LocalTime|20:00|tz=UTC+1|day=Saturday}} {{LocalTime|20:00|to=22:00|tz=UTC+1}} {{LocalTime|18:30}} The first parameter is the time, as HH:MM on a 24 hour clock. tz (optional) is the time zone the time is given in. Use UTC (the default) or an offset like UTC+1, UTC-5 or UTC+5:30. day (optional) is a weekday in English (Monday to Sunday). The reader's local weekday is shown too, because a time can land on another day for them. to (optional) is the end time, to show a range like 21:00–23:00. Hovering the time shows how it was originally written. Needs the script Common.js (the block "Local times"). A time that is shown in the reader's own time zone. html:
Writes a time that changes to the reader's own time zone. Someone in New York and someone in Stockholm both see the time in their own clock. Without JavaScript, or while the page loads, the time is shown as it was typed with its time zone.

Usage 

{{LocalTime|20:00|tz=UTC+1|day=Saturday}}
{{LocalTime|20:00|to=22:00|tz=UTC+1}}
{{LocalTime|18:30}}
  • The first parameter is the time, as HH:MM on a 24 hour clock.
  • tz (optional) is the time zone the time is given in. Use UTC (the default) or an offset like UTC+1, UTC-5 or UTC+5:30.
  • day (optional) is a weekday in English (Monday to Sunday). The reader's local weekday is shown too, because a time can land on another day for them.
  • to (optional) is the end time, to show a range like 21:00–23:00.
  • Hovering the time shows how it was originally written.
  • Needs the script Common.js (the block "Local times").

A time that is shown in the reader's own time zone.
